items.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022
items.q: I had a rehearsal band with some good arrangements... Bobby Porcelli, great alto player. He would get the saxophones.

ctx.x: What kind of gig do you like to play now that has sort of no pressure. Like when you’re doing “Chicago” every night you just have to be so focused. What kind of gig is the total opposite of that for you?

Boy that’s a good question man. Well actually I had a rehearsal band with some good arrangements and that was fun. I would call a rehearsal, I’d call up the guys, great players, everybody would always say yes I’ll be there, for no money, for two hours maybe in between shows. And we’d play whatever I’d call up. I was the leader. Let’s © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

play #23 you know. And man, like it was, after that two hours, first of all everybody always showed up. Nobody canceled or anything. I mean great players man. Bobby Porcelli, great alto player. He would get the saxophones. And man like just all great players man. And they would want to play longer. I only had the room for two hours.
